By the Rashevskii–Chow theorem (Coron, Theorems 3.18 and 3.19) the nonholonomic integrator is therefore globally and small-time locally controllable, even though its…
nodes.title: The nonholonomic integrator satisfies the Lie algebra rank condition

nodes.summary: For the driftless control-affine system $\dot x = \sum_{i=1}^m u_i f_i(x)$, the accessibility space at $x$ is the span of the values at $x$ of the fields $f_i$ and of all their iterated Lie brackets, that is, $\{ g(x) : g \in \operatorname{Lie}(\{f_1, \dots, f_m\}) \}$ (Coron, *Control and Nonlinearity*, AMS 2007, Definition 3.13 and the formula for $A(x_e, u_e)$ before Definition 3.16, at $u_e = 0$). The Lie…
nodes.title: Accessibility space of a driftless system at a point

nodes.summary: Let $E$ and $U$ be finite-dimensional real normed spaces and $f : E \times U \to E$ of class $C^\infty$ with $f(0, 0) = 0$. If $\dot x = f(x, u)$ is locally asymptotically stabilisable by continuous stationary feedback laws, then the image under $f$ of every neighbourhood of $(0, 0)$ is a neighbourhood of $0$.
nodes.title: Brockett's necessary condition for stabilisation

nodes.summary: A map $f : E \times U \to E$ satisfies Brockett's condition if the image under $f$ of every neighbourhood of $(0, 0)$ is a neighbourhood of $0$ in $E$ (Coron, *Control and Nonlinearity*, AMS 2007, Theorem 11.1, after Brockett 1983). For $f(0, 0) = 0$ this is necessary for local asymptotic stabilisation of $\dot x = f(x, u)$ by continuous stationary feedback.
nodes.title: Brockett's condition

nodes.summary: The control system $\dot x = f(x, u)$, $f : E \times U \to E$, is locally asymptotically stabilisable by continuous stationary feedback laws if there is a continuous $u : E \to U$ with $u(0) = 0$ such that $0$ is locally asymptotically stable for the closed-loop system $\dot x = f(x, u(x))$ (Coron, *Control and Nonlinearity*, AMS 2007, Definition 10.11). "Stationary" distinguishes these feedback laws from the…
nodes.title: Stabilisability by continuous stationary feedback

nodes.summary: Let $X : E \to E$ be a vector field on a real normed space. The origin is locally asymptotically stable for $\dot x = X(x)$ if there is $\delta > 0$ such that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $M > 0$ with $\lVert x(t) \rVert < \varepsilon$ for every solution $x$ of $\dot x = X(x)$ with $\lVert x(0) \rVert < \delta$ and every time $t > M$ in its interval of definition.
nodes.title: Local asymptotic stability of an equilibrium of a continuous vector field

nodes.summary: For vector fields $f_1, \dots, f_m$ on a real normed space $E$, the set of iterated Lie brackets is the smallest set of vector fields containing every $f_i$ and closed under the Lie bracket This is the sign convention of Coron, *Control and Nonlinearity* (AMS 2007), Definition 3.10, and of Mathlib's `VectorField.lieBracket`. For smooth fields, the linear span of the iterated brackets is the Lie algebra…
nodes.title: Iterated Lie brackets of a family of vector fields

nodes.summary: At every $x \in \mathbb{R}^3$, $f_1, f_2 = Df_2(x) f_1(x) - Df_1(x) f_2(x) = (0, 0, 2)$ (Coron, *Control and Nonlinearity*, AMS 2007, Example 3.20, with his bracket convention of Definition 3.10). Both fields are affine, so their derivatives are constant: $Df_2(x) v = (0, 0, v_1)$ and $Df_1(x) v = (0, 0, -v_2)$.
nodes.title: The bracket of the nonholonomic integrator

nodes.summary: The vector fields $f_1(x) = (1, 0, -x_2)$ and $f_2(x) = (0, 1, x_1)$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$ (Coron, *Control and Nonlinearity*, AMS 2007, Example 3.20). Coordinates are indexed from $0$ in Lean.
nodes.title: Vector fields of the nonholonomic integrator

nodes.summary: The nonholonomic integrator is the driftless control-affine system $f(x, u) = u_1 f_1(x) + u_2 f_2(x)$ defined by its two vector fields (Coron, *Control and Nonlinearity*, AMS 2007, (3.41) and Example 3.20).
nodes.title: The nonholonomic integrator as a driftless system

nodes.summary: The nonholonomic integrator is the control system $\dot x_1 = u_1$, $\dot x_2 = u_2$, $\dot x_3 = x_1 u_2 - x_2 u_1$ with state $x \in \mathbb{R}^3$ and control $u \in \mathbb{R}^2$ (Coron, *Control and Nonlinearity*, AMS 2007, (3.41) and (11.4); Brockett 1983). It is the driftless system $u_1 f_1 + u_2 f_2$ with $f_1(x) = (1, 0, -x_2)$ and $f_2(x) = (0, 1, x_1)$, whose bracket $[f_1, f_2] = (0, 0, 2)$ completes…
nodes.title: The nonholonomic integrator

nodes.summary: No point $(0, 0, \eta)$ with $\eta \ne 0$ is a value of the nonholonomic integrator $f(x, u) = (u_1, u_2, x_1 u_2 - x_2 u_1)$: the first two coordinates force $u = 0$, and then the third vanishes. So even the image of the whole space is not a neighbourhood of $0$, and Brockett's condition fails (Coron, *Control and Nonlinearity*, AMS 2007, Example 11.2, after Brockett 1983). nodes.title: The nonholonomic integrator violates Brockett's condition

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
